overview.summary: Hotel managers run the daily operations of a hotel so that guests have a comfortable, safe and enjoyable stay.
overview.problems: They coordinate rooms, food, cleaning, maintenance and staff, and solve problems for guests quickly.
overview.worksWith: Guests, front desk, housekeeping, kitchen and restaurant staff, maintenance teams, suppliers and owners.
overview.workplaces: Hotels, resorts and guesthouses of all sizes, and some work in serviced apartments or hospitality groups.

timeline.title: Review the day
timeline.description: The manager checks arrivals, departures, occupancy, events and any overnight issues.
timeline.why: The day's plan depends on who is arriving.

timeline.title: Walk around the hotel
timeline.description: The manager checks the lobby, rooms, restaurant and facilities and talks with staff.
timeline.why: Seeing the guest experience first-hand reveals problems.

timeline.title: Meeting guests and staff
timeline.description: The manager welcomes guests, handles requests and complaints, and briefs teams.
timeline.why: Guests remember how problems are handled.

timeline.title: Managing budgets and bookings
timeline.description: The manager checks costs, prices, supplier orders and reviews.
timeline.why: Hotels must manage money and reputation.

timeline.title: Peak service
timeline.description: The manager supports the busiest period, with check-ins, dinner service and events.
timeline.why: Leaders are most needed when the hotel is busiest.

timeline.title: Out-of-hours problems
timeline.description: Hotels are open all night, so problems can occur at any hour.
timeline.why: Guests expect help at any time.

responsibilities: Making sure the hotel is safe, clean and follows regulations
challenges: Hours are long and irregular, including evenings, weekends and holidays.
Some guests are demanding or upset.
Staff shortages and high turnover affect some places.
Quality has to be balanced with cost.
Responsibility for guests' safety and the hotel's reputation is serious.
Entry roles may start with low pay.
workEnvironment: Hotels and resorts that are open 24 hours a day, with a lot of time on your feet, talking to guests and staff. Hours often include evenings, weekends and holidays. Managers move between the front desk, restaurant and back offices.
rewards: Variety, and meeting people from many places
Career paths in hospitality around the world
tradeoffs: Pay and conditions that vary by country, location and size of hotel

activity.title: Plan a stay for a pretend guest
steps: Imagine your home is a small guesthouse and write a profile of a guest.
Make a one-page welcome guide with check-in time, Wi-Fi, local places and emergency contacts.
Write a checklist for preparing a room.
Ask a family member to be the guest and give feedback.
Note whether looking after others felt rewarding.
activity.outcome: You practise planning, being organized and putting yourself in a guest's place.
activity.safety: Do not share your real home address or private details outside the family, and do not invite strangers.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
